description: We are a passionate team interested in AI, Machine Learning, Data Science, and Space Exploration. Our goal is to turn innovative ideas into practical solutions using technology, creativity, and collaboration. We have interests in Python, software development, data analysis, and cybersecurity. We welcome enthusiastic people with skills in astronomy, satellite data, AI/ML, statistics, hardware, IoT, web development, and design. No need to be an expert—curiosity and teamwork matter most!
summary:
NEBULA X – The Forgotten Space Archive

NEBULA X is an interactive educational space-archaeology experience that brings attention to the scientific equipment and spacecraft humanity has left behind during space exploration.

Through an immersive 3D Solar System experience, users can explore three destinations: the Moon, Mars, and Deep Space. They can discover historical missions, inspect abandoned equipment, understand its original purpose, explore scientific contributions, and learn what happened to each mission.

The platform combines 3D visualization, NASA/NSSDCA source-referenced mission records, narrated storytelling, evidence inspection, interactive quizzes, comparison tools, and educational activities.

Features such as the Evidence Scanner, Mission Control, Comparison Lab, Student Field Guide, and downloadable achievement certificate make space history engaging and accessible.

Our mission is to preserve the stories behind humanity's space exploration achievements and remind people that even when a mission ends, its scientific legacy remains.
details:
NEBULA X 2.0 – The Forgotten Space Archive

PROBLEM AND PURPOSE

Humanity's exploration of space has left behind numerous spacecraft, scientific instruments, landers, rovers, and other equipment on the Moon, Mars, and beyond. Although many missions have ended, their equipment and scientific contributions remain important parts of space exploration history.

However, these objects are often overlooked, and their stories can be difficult for students and the general public to explore.

NEBULA X addresses this problem by transforming space mission archives into an interactive educational space-archaeology experience.

HOW THE PROJECT WORKS

NEBULA X provides an interactive 3D Solar System environment where users can explore three major destinations: the Moon, Mars, and Deep Space.

Users can select destinations, inspect equipment markers, navigate 3D scenes, and explore structured mission records. Each equipment record provides information about the mission, equipment identity, historical context, scientific contributions, evidence, timelines, and source references.

The platform currently organizes 13 equipment groups across the three destination categories.

KEY FEATURES

  1. 3D Solar System Exploration:
    Users can navigate an interactive 3D environment, select destinations, and inspect equipment markers.
  2. Evidence Scanner:
    Users can inspect equipment records and scan evidence to earn exploration experience points.
  3. Narrated Equipment Stories:
    Users can read or listen to educational stories about historical space equipment and access transcripts.
  4. Mission Control:
    An interactive quiz helps students test their knowledge and retain learning progress.
  5. Comparison Lab:
    Users can compare different spacecraft and equipment groups.
  6. Student Field Guide:
    Educational questions and explanations help students understand the scientific and historical importance of each equipment group.
  7. Image Inspector:
    Users can inspect associated NASA mission images.
  8. Earth Connection:
    Each equipment record explains its connection to Earth and its scientific significance.
  9. Achievement Certificate:
    Users can generate and download a visual certificate as a PNG or print it as a PDF.
  10. Scientific Evidence and Source References:
    The platform distinguishes documented facts, scientific interpretations, and educational dramatizations. Source metadata helps users identify the archival basis behind mission information.

TECHNOLOGIES USED

Frontend:

  • React
  • React DOM
  • JavaScript
  • Vite
  • CSS

3D Visualization:

  • Three.js
  • React Three Fiber
  • @react-three/drei

Additional Libraries and Technologies:

  • Lucide React for interface icons
  • Canvas 2D for certificate generation
  • Browser LocalStorage for saving exploration and quiz progress
  • Node.js built-in testing tools

DATA AND SCIENTIFIC INTEGRITY

The project uses NASA and NASA/NSSDCA archival information to organize its mission records. Its structured mission data includes source references, archival identifiers, verification information, and content classifications.

Documented facts are separated from scientific interpretations and educational dramatizations. This approach helps prevent fictional storytelling from being mistaken for verified historical information.

The project also includes scientific-integrity documentation, a NASA source-verification matrix, educational quality reports, and automated tests for important data and application rules.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

NEBULA X is designed for students, educators, space enthusiasts, and anyone interested in space exploration.

It makes historical space equipment easier to understand through interactive visualization and educational storytelling. It encourages curiosity, scientific thinking, evidence-based learning, and appreciation of the engineering achievements behind space missions.

CREATIVITY AND INNOVATION

Instead of presenting abandoned spacecraft as a simple list of historical objects, NEBULA X transforms them into an interactive space archive.

The combination of 3D exploration, evidence inspection, narrated stories, student activities, mission comparisons, and source-referenced information creates an educational experience that connects technology, science, and storytelling.

Our central idea is that a mission does not lose its importance when it ends. Its discoveries, engineering achievements, and scientific contributions remain part of humanity's journey into space.
